object.title: Google’s secret iCal address: subscribe without confusing it with sharing
object.description: Understand Google’s secret iCal address, account connections and shared feeds. Handle an exposed address without promising instant updates or erased copies.
object.lede: A calendar address, an account connection and an invitation do different jobs. Identify which one you have before using it to bring a schedule into another application. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
object.commonBelief: A secret calendar address is a personal invitation that can be withdrawn from just one recipient.

sections.heading: Choose the connection for the job
body: Google distinguishes signing in to another calendar application from viewing through a secret iCal address. The account route can support editing; the address provides a view-only subscription. Google describes the secret address as being for your own use and advises against sharing it with other people.

For example, displaying your own work schedule in another compatible calendar is different from giving a colleague ongoing access. Start with the outcome: viewing your schedule, collaborating with a named person, or distributing an audience-facing timetable. Do not choose a URL merely because it is easy to paste.

sections.heading: Find the correct calendar, not just the correct account
body: On a computer, Google’s instructions place “Secret address in iCal format” under the chosen calendar’s “Integrate calendar” settings. Check the calendar name first. Work or school administrators may restrict this option; an absent address is not a reason to publish the calendar instead.

Keep the address out of screenshots, public support posts and shared notes. When requesting help, describe the account type, calendar name and connection method without supplying the URL. A support conversation normally needs to identify the route before it needs any event content.

sections.heading: Check what the receiving application actually added
body: A subscription follows a feed; an imported file creates a separate copy. Read the receiving application’s instructions and confirm which action you are taking. If you simply open a downloaded calendar file, do not assume the resulting appointments will follow later changes.

Check which app actually opens the link and which account its subscription setup shows. In Apple Calendar, Apple’s instructions select iCloud in Account and use the same Apple Account on the devices intended to show that subscription. After saving, look for the named calendar in the receiving app’s calendar list and select it for viewing. An opened link alone does not confirm that a subscription was saved or that Cloud Calendars can display it.

Use an ordinary, non-sensitive event you already recognise to compare the calendar name, date and displayed details. Avoid creating a second subscription to diagnose the first: two visible copies can make a delayed update look like a conflicting appointment. Hide one calendar temporarily when identifying the source.

sections.heading: Keep Google and Cloud Calendars links separate
body: Cloud Calendars has its own event and calendar sharing flows, including subscription feeds. Those are not Google secret addresses. Establish whether the sender shared one event, a calendar, or an account-based invitation before choosing how to open it. A Google secret iCal address belongs in a compatible app’s external-subscription flow; it is not a Cloud Calendars invitation link.

A Cloud Calendars recipient can have a Reader, Writer or Owner role. A feed address alone should not be treated as proof of editing rights. Likewise, receiving a Google viewing address does not make you the owner of its calendar. Ask the sender which system should be used for changes.

sections.heading: Allow for the receiving calendar’s refresh behavior
body: A subscription is not a promise of immediate delivery. Cloud Calendars feeds include a suggested refresh interval, but the receiving application decides when it retrieves and displays updates. An old time on one device does not by itself prove that the organiser failed to save the change.

For a same-day meeting, compare with the organiser’s current schedule and confirm important changes directly. Record which calendar still shows the old information and when you checked it. Do not repeatedly import the event or delete the source calendar to force a feed to catch up.

sections.heading: Respond to exposure without promising a recall
body: Google documents resetting a disclosed secret address, which invalidates the old address and creates a replacement. Identify your own applications that use it so you can update their subscriptions afterward. Resetting an address is a different action from removing a named collaborator.

Previously saved appointments, exports or screenshots are a separate matter. A changed link cannot demonstrate that every earlier copy has disappeared. If you distributed information to the wrong audience, consider the actual material and recipients rather than treating a successful reset as proof of complete removal.

practical: Identify whether you have an account connection, invitation, subscription or file.
Check the owning calendar before copying an address.
Keep a Google secret address for your own compatible applications.
Verify which app and account received the calendar, and that it subscribed rather than imported. Check the named calendar and a known event before adding anything again.
Confirm urgent changes with the organiser instead of relying on refresh timing.
If a secret address was exposed, follow Google’s reset guidance and update intended connections.

faq.q: Can I give the secret address to a colleague?
faq.a: Google advises keeping it for your own applications. Use the calendar’s sharing controls when another person needs access, choosing the intended permission.

faq.q: Will a subscription let me edit the original?
faq.a: A Google secret iCal address is a viewing route. Editing needs a suitable account connection and permission; Cloud Calendars sharing roles are a separate arrangement.

faq.q: Does resetting the address erase old appointments everywhere?
faq.a: It invalidates the old Google address. It does not establish that independently saved files, appointments or screenshots have been removed.

object.title: Stop sharing a calendar: remove access and check the remaining routes
object.description: Stop calendar sharing without confusing people, groups, public access and feed links. Check what changed and understand why saved copies may remain.
object.lede: Ending a collaboration starts with identifying how access was granted. Removing a person, disabling publication and resetting a feed address are different actions. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
object.commonBelief: Removing one recipient instantly recalls every calendar copy and closes every other route to the schedule.

sections.heading: Identify the calendar and the sharing route
body: Confirm the owning account, calendar and intended audience before changing access. A Google calendar shared with a named colleague is a different relationship from a public calendar, a group grant or a subscription address. Cloud Calendars also has its own event and calendar sharing relationships.

For example, a club secretary may receive editing rights through a named invitation while members follow a published schedule. Removing the secretary’s named grant does not describe what should happen to the members’ subscriptions. Make a list of the arrangements you actually created.

sections.heading: Remove the intended Google grant
body: Google documents separate controls for named people or groups, organisation-wide sharing and public availability. On a computer, open the intended calendar’s sharing settings and change the relevant entry or broader setting. Check the signed-in account and calendar name first.

A person may still have another access route, such as a group or broader publication. Review the whole arrangement instead of repeating removal of one email address. Work or school policies may limit the available controls; use the owner or administrator’s approved process when necessary.

sections.heading: Treat a secret calendar address separately
body: Google says its secret iCal address is for your own use in another calendar application and should not be given to other people. If it was disclosed, Google documents resetting it to invalidate the old address. That is a different action from removing a named person.

Before changing a subscription address you use yourself, identify the calendar clients or tools that depend on it so you can reconnect the intended ones afterward. Do not paste the secret URL into a public support post or send it as evidence that you found the correct calendar. Refer to the calendar name and the type of connection instead.

sections.heading: Distinguish Cloud Calendars recipients from feed links
body: In Cloud Calendars, event or calendar recipient access and an issued subscription feed are distinct mechanisms. Review the actual event or calendar sharing relationship and the relevant link before choosing an action. Removing an identified recipient is not a blanket promise that every previously distributed URL or independent copy has been recalled.

If a co-organizer only needs to stop editing, consider the intended role and remaining audience instead of deleting the shared schedule. If the whole collaboration is ending, establish who owns the calendar and who should retain it. Leaving a received calendar and deleting a calendar you own are different decisions.

sections.heading: Verify the result without promising immediate disappearance
body: Check that the intended change is saved in the owning system. If an authorised colleague can help, confirm the relevant viewing or editing result from their own account without sharing passwords. Distinguish an access denial from an old event still visible in a cached or imported copy.

Do not promise a universal refresh interval or that no notification will be sent. For a group handover, communicate which schedule should be used from now on. A visible old record does not by itself identify whether the person retains live access, has another grant or kept a standalone copy.

sections.heading: Handle previous copies as a separate follow-up
body: Previously exported files, screenshots, messages and independently saved appointments may remain after access changes. Decide which copies matter for the handover and discuss their handling with the people involved. Changing a calendar permission cannot establish what every recipient has already saved.

Keep necessary source records while reviewing the outcome. Do not move sensitive meetings into another shared calendar simply to make the old one look empty, or cancel real invitations as an access test. Record the calendar, route and change you made so later troubleshooting has a clear starting point.

practical: Identify the owning account, calendar and sharing route.
Review named people, groups and broader publication separately.
Use the appropriate Google or Cloud Calendars sharing controls.
Handle a disclosed secret feed address as a separate reset decision.
Verify the saved access result without sharing credentials.
Plan for previous exports or copies separately from live access.

faq.q: Does removing one person disable a public calendar or their group access?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Review each actual route. Google documents named recipients, groups and broader publication as separate settings.

faq.q: Will the calendar disappear immediately and silently?
faq.a: There is no universal promise here about disappearance, notification or refresh timing. Confirm the saved access change and distinguish live access from cached or imported information.

faq.q: Does Advanced buy the ability to remove Google calendar access?
faq.a: Advanced removes ads in Cloud Calendars. Google sharing controls depend on ownership, permissions and organisation rules, rather than that app plan.

object.title: Disconnect a calendar integration: access, sync and existing copies
object.description: Separate calendar sign-out, provider access and existing copies. Check Cloud Calendars account routes before disconnecting or removing a calendar.
object.lede: Stopping a connection and removing its calendar copies are different decisions. Identify the route you use and preserve needed information before choosing a disconnect action. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
object.commonBelief: Signing out only pauses updates, revokes every related permission and leaves all existing calendar data exactly as it was.

sections.heading: Identify the connection you intend to stop
body: Start with the account and calendar that own the events. A provider account added through iPhone settings, a direct connection in Cloud Calendars, an iCalendar subscription and the app’s sharing identity are separate routes. The same email address does not make their controls interchangeable.

Write down the calendar names and which route displays them, without sharing private event details. Decide whether your aim is to stop future access, leave a shared arrangement or remove a copy. If you are investigating a missing or duplicate event, disconnecting is not the first diagnostic step.

sections.heading: Check what the app’s sign-out action removes
body: The implementation reviewed for this guide attempts to disconnect the selected Google calendar profile and remove its mapped calendar copies from the iOS calendar store. Treat this as a removal action, not a pause. A connection error can still occur, so check the provider’s access status separately rather than assuming every permission was revoked.

The Microsoft calendar-profile sign-out path also attempts to remove its mapped calendars and local connection records. Do not assume those copies will remain visible. Calendar-copy storage can depend on the device’s available sources, so check the source and preserve needed information before proceeding.

sections.heading: Review future access at the provider separately
body: Google’s linked-app controls distinguish Sign in with Google from access to Google Account data. Review the intended app, account and link type. Removing the relevant data access and stopping a sign-in link answer different questions; an app-level sign-out alone is not proof that every connection is gone.

For a Microsoft work or school account, Microsoft documents My Apps > Manage your application to review permissions. You can revoke permissions you personally granted, but administrator-granted access needs the organisation’s administrator. This is work-or-school guidance, not a universal procedure for personal Microsoft accounts.

sections.heading: Separate a sharing identity from calendar-provider sync
body: Cloud Calendars also has an account used for sharing. Its current source treats signing out of that account separately from the calendar-profile connections: it clears the local sharing session and reduces locally tracked shared access to reader status. That is not a declaration that all server data has been deleted.

When multiple sharing identities are linked, disconnecting one retains the account through another identity. With the final identity, the current path signs out locally and leaves the server link for recovery. Do not use signing out as a substitute for a data-deletion request or assume it also disconnects every calendar provider.

sections.heading: Handle subscriptions and previous copies by their own rules
body: Apple documents unsubscribing from an external calendar separately from selecting which calendars to display. If the item is a read-only subscription, identify that subscription before using its unsubscribe control. Hiding a calendar, unsubscribing from a feed and deleting an editable calendar are different operations.

Google notes that removing an app’s access may still require a separate request to delete data the developer already holds. Likewise, a previously exported file or another person’s copy is not recalled by a permission switch. Keep privacy or retention follow-up separate from whether new updates are still authorised.

sections.heading: Confirm the outcome before cleaning up anything else
body: After an intentional change, check the provider’s connection status and compare the original calendar with the app. Identify what stopped updating, what disappeared locally and what remains elsewhere. Do not delete lookalike events merely because a connection name no longer appears.

If the result is unexpected, stop further cleanup and contact support with the account route, calendar source and the action you used. Do not send passwords, access tokens, private feed URLs or screenshots of sensitive appointments. Explain whether the original provider calendar still has the events so support can distinguish a connection problem from a missing copy.

practical: Identify the exact account, calendar and connection route.
Decide whether you want to stop access, leave sharing or remove a copy.
Preserve needed information through a verified export or backup route.
Read what the installed sign-out or disconnect action removes before using it.
Review provider permissions separately; involve an administrator for managed access.
Check the result at the provider and app before any further cleanup.

faq.q: Does signing out of a direct Cloud Calendars connection keep its calendar copies?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The inspected Google and Microsoft calendar-profile paths attempt to remove their mapped calendars from the iOS store. Review the source and preserve needed information before disconnecting.

faq.q: Does removing an app’s Google access delete data it already copied?
faq.a: Google says you may need to request deletion of data already held by the developer separately. Review future access and retained data as different outcomes.

faq.q: Is signing out of the sharing account the same as deleting it?
faq.a: No. The current sharing path clears a local session and retains recovery behaviour; it is separate from the calendar-provider sign-out paths and is not proof of server-data deletion.

object.title: Google Calendar guest permissions: editing, invitations and the guest list
object.description: Check Google event guest permissions and defaults. Separate invitation rights from calendar access and Cloud Calendars Reader, Writer and Owner roles.
object.lede: A guest’s ability to reply does not describe everything they can do. Review the event’s permissions before using one invitation for a team, clients or a public gathering. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
object.commonBelief: Invited guests can only accept or decline, and every application exposes the same permission controls.

sections.heading: Begin with the organiser and the original event
body: Open the intended event in Google Calendar using the organising account, or an account authorised to manage it. Check its calendar, date and organiser before changing permissions. A separately imported appointment is not a reliable place to control the original invitation.

For a team meeting, write down the intended arrangement: who may reschedule it, who may bring others, and whether participants should see one another. These are separate decisions. A guest who needs to attend does not necessarily need to manage the meeting.

sections.heading: Decide whether guests should modify the meeting
body: Google documents a “Modify event” option under “Guests can” in its computer event editor. This is a broad collaboration permission, not merely a way to suggest a new time. Google explains that it enables event management including editing fields, viewing guests and booking rooms.

For example, a trusted co-organiser arranging a workshop may need that flexibility. A customer attending an appointment may not. Choose based on the responsibility you are giving the guest, and verify the saved event rather than relying on how a different meeting was configured.

sections.heading: Review invitations and guest visibility separately
body: Google’s event model distinguishes permission to invite others from permission to see other guests. Review both alongside editing access. Turning off one capability does not mean you have checked the other, and a displayed default is not evidence of the settings on an existing event.

For a gathering of unrelated clients, consider whether one shared invitation is appropriate at all. Information already included in an email, description or forwarded message is outside the narrow question of the current guest-list control. Do not put confidential participant details in a description and expect a hidden list to conceal them.

sections.heading: Check defaults as well as important individual events
body: Google also documents “Default guest permissions” in its Event settings, including a default for modification. The controls are therefore not exclusively an event-by-event matter. Review your defaults when your usual scheduling pattern changes, then check significant existing invitations individually.

For a recurring meeting, confirm which occurrence or series you are editing before saving. Do not assume that changing a preference has rewritten older invitations. When testing an arrangement with a colleague, use an agreed, non-sensitive example instead of moving or cancelling a real customer meeting.

sections.heading: Check document access separately from meeting access
body: A guest who can see the meeting may still be unable to open its document. Google stores event attachments in Drive and checks the file’s sharing permissions separately. A filename can be visible even when the file itself is inaccessible. Identify the original event, the intended recipient account and the attached file before changing calendar permissions.

For a workshop, a participant may receive the invitation yet still need access to the agenda. Have the file owner review its Drive sharing for the intended audience and let the participant check again with the intended account. Do not publish a work document or broaden the whole calendar merely to resolve the error. If the attachment control is unavailable, check the organising Google identity and whether the organisation enables Drive. Cloud Calendars Reader, Writer and Owner roles do not establish Google Drive access.

sections.heading: Keep Cloud Calendars roles distinct
body: Cloud Calendars has a separate sharing arrangement with Reader, Writer and Owner roles. Reader provides viewing and syncing; Writer permits editing; Owner also manages sharing and access with the invited identity. These roles should not be presented as switches for Google’s three guest permissions.

When a Google-specific permission matters, inspect the original event in Google Calendar. Seeing an attendee in Cloud Calendars does not establish that every Google guest setting can be changed there. Keep the owning service and the recipient’s identity clear when diagnosing a missing control or an unsuccessful edit.

sections.heading: Verify the saved outcome and communicate responsibility
body: After saving, reopen the original event and check the intended settings. Where appropriate, ask an authorised colleague to confirm what their own account can do. Do not exchange passwords or send private guest details as a shortcut for checking access.

Keep attendance separate from permissions. A person’s ability to edit, an imported copy, and a recorded acceptance are different facts. In Cloud Calendars, a sharing receipt is not an RSVP. For an important meeting, ask for the attendance response you need and make clear who is responsible for schedule changes.

practical: Identify the organising account and original event.
Decide who should manage the meeting, invite others and see guests.
Inspect the Google event’s actual guest permissions.
Review Google defaults without assuming they change existing events.
Check attached documents in Google Drive with the intended recipient account; calendar access alone does not establish file access.
Treat Cloud Calendars sharing roles as a separate permission system.
Reopen the saved event and confirm attendance separately.

faq.q: Can a guest change my meeting time?
faq.a: Google supports granting modification permission. Check the actual event and the guest’s access; do not infer it from the fact that they received an invitation.

faq.q: Are all guest permissions configured only on each event?
faq.a: No. Google documents default guest permissions as well. Check defaults for future scheduling and inspect important existing events themselves.

faq.q: Does hiding the guest list remove information already sent?
faq.a: It does not demonstrate that earlier emails, descriptions, screenshots or independent copies were removed. Review what was actually distributed separately.

faq.q: Why can a guest see the filename but not open the attachment?
faq.a: Google can show an attachment’s filename to people who can see the event details even when they cannot open the file. Check the file’s Google Drive sharing and the recipient’s intended account. Ask the file owner to review access rather than granting broader calendar permissions or publishing the document.

object.title: Calendar replies: separate attendance from sharing access
object.short: Who replied and who has access
object.description: Distinguish guest RSVPs from pending invitations, anonymous recipients and shared-calendar acceptance. Confirm attendance without inventing a headcount.
object.lede: A person can open a link, add an event or accept calendar access without promising to attend. Decide which answer you need before interpreting a recipient list. This guide is written by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
object.commonBelief: Everyone recorded as a recipient or accepted share is a confirmed attendee, and silence can be converted into a reliable estimate.

sections.heading: Identify the kind of invitation
body: A provider meeting invitation asks a guest for an attendance response. A Cloud Calendars share gives someone access to event details or a calendar, possibly with editing rights. An ICS subscription follows information. These actions can concern the same meeting without recording the same decision.

For example, a volunteer may accept Writer access to update an event but not attend it. A guest may read the details in a web preview and then reply by message. Neither case should be counted solely from an access-management screen.

sections.heading: Read sharing recipients as access information
body: Cloud Calendars recipient information distinguishes pending email invitations, identified recipients, anonymous recipients and access roles. A pending invitation may offer a resend action. Reader, Writer and Owner describe what the recipient can do with shared information.

The sharing system records acceptance or receipt during its add/access flows. That record is useful for understanding the sharing relationship, but it is not a Yes/Maybe/No attendance answer. Anonymous reception also does not identify a named guest for your headcount.

sections.heading: Check attendance in the organizer’s invitation workflow
body: For a Google meeting invitation, Google documents explicit Yes, No and Maybe responses. Apple Calendar likewise distinguishes Accept, Maybe and Decline for supported invitations. Use the organizer’s corresponding event and account when checking those replies.

If a reply looks wrong or missing, confirm the invited email and the event version with the person. An imported copy, a forwarded link or an event in another account may not represent the original invitation. Do not assume that every third-party display has the latest response.

sections.heading: Keep unknown attendance unknown
body: A pending share, no response or an unread message is not a reliable acceptance or refusal. Record the people who explicitly confirmed, those who declined and those whose answer is still unknown. Do not add a fixed fraction of silent recipients to the confirmed total.

For a meal with a booking deadline, state the date by which you need a reply and ask the remaining people directly. The appropriate follow-up depends on the event; there is no universal rule that one reminder two days before is enough.

sections.heading: Treat meeting links as joining details
body: A Google Meet or Microsoft Teams URL tells someone where to join, not whether they accepted or will attend. Cloud Calendars lists Google Meet with Base features and Microsoft Teams with Premium, subject to the relevant account and provider flow. A higher plan is not a more reliable attendance count.

Check that the intended link exists on the event and works for the intended audience. File imports and other conversions can lose conference information. If you change the meeting arrangement, tell participants which event and link to use instead of interpreting their old access record as confirmation.

sections.heading: Close the loop after an important change
body: When an event moves substantially, update it through its owning calendar or sharing flow. Then tell the people whose attendance matters and ask for renewed confirmation where needed. A previous response to Tuesday is not necessarily an answer to Thursday.

Keep the final attendance list separate from the access list. Removing editing rights does not cancel a guest’s attendance, and declining shared access does not necessarily decline the underlying gathering. Use clear messages so people know which decision you are asking them to make.

practical: Identify whether you sent a provider meeting invitation, an app share or a feed.
Use the sharing list to check access and pending invitations, not attendance totals.
Check provider RSVP status on the organizer’s actual event where applicable.
Keep unknown replies separate from confirmed and declined guests.
Ask for a direct answer by a deadline appropriate to your event.
After a major change, confirm the new arrangement and joining link with affected guests.

faq.q: Does accepted calendar access mean the person is coming?
faq.a: No. It means a sharing relationship was accepted through that flow. Attendance needs a provider RSVP or an explicit answer from the person.

faq.q: Can I count anonymous recipients as confirmed guests?
faq.a: No. Anonymous reception is not an identified attendance commitment. It may help describe use of a shared event, but it cannot supply a reliable named guest list.

faq.q: Do I need Premium to know who replied?
faq.a: Do not equate an app tier with RSVP reliability. Premium adds Microsoft Calendar and Teams features; access receipts and provider attendance responses remain different kinds of information. Check the original invitation and organizer account.
